_meta.note: 原创角色声线，不模仿或克隆任何真实人物。

Mom.instruct: A warm American woman in her early thirties with a gentle, caring voice. Speak natural standard American English with relaxed conversational rhythm, clear pronunciation for young learners, and subtle emotion. Avoid announcer cadence, robotic pacing, exaggerated acting, or sing-song delivery.

Dad.instruct: A friendly American father with a calm, reassuring mid-range voice. Speak natural standard American English, relaxed and encouraging, with clear everyday pronunciation for young learners. Avoid announcer cadence, robotic pacing, exaggerated acting, or sing-song delivery.

Mia.instruct: An American girl around eight to ten years old with an unmistakably young, bright, friendly voice. Speak natural standard American English a little slower than ordinary conversation. Articulate every word clearly for beginning English learners, with crisp consonants, complete word endings, gentle pauses, and cheerful childlike energy. Sound like a real little girl, not a teenager or adult. Keep the performance warm and natural, never cartoonish, squeaky, breathy, robotic, exaggerated, or sing-song.

Ben.instruct: A friendly school-age American boy with a clear, sunny voice. Speak natural standard American English with relaxed confidence, age-appropriate conversational rhythm, and clear pronunciation. Keep the performance genuine and restrained, never cartoonish, robotic, or sing-song.

Child.instruct: A cheerful school-age American child with a warm, natural voice. Speak standard American English with relaxed everyday rhythm and clear pronunciation for fellow young learners. Keep the performance genuine and restrained, never cartoonish, robotic, or sing-song.

Teacher.instruct: A kind American elementary-school teacher with a warm, patient voice. Speak natural standard American English, clearly but conversationally, with calm encouragement. Avoid announcer cadence, robotic pacing, exaggerated acting, or sing-song delivery.

default.instruct: A friendly native speaker of standard American English. Speak naturally and conversationally with clear pronunciation for young learners. Avoid announcer cadence, robotic pacing, exaggerated acting, or sing-song delivery.
